examples.en: I almost tripped on the threshold.
The child is standing on the threshold.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 문지방을 밟으면 복이 나간다고 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, people said that stepping on the threshold makes good luck leave.
The threshold is high, so it's hard for a wheelchair to get in.

examples.ko: 문지방 위에 앉지 말고 안으로 들어오세요.
examples.en: Don't sit on the threshold; come inside.
My foot caught on the threshold and I hurt my toe.

explain: '문턱'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '문턱'이 더 흔해요. '문지방을 밟지 마라'처럼 어른들이 하는 옛말에 자주 나와요. 비유로 쓰는 '문턱이 높다'(들어가기 어렵다)는 '문턱'과 같이 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 그는 그 가게를 문지방이 닳도록 드나들었어요.
phrases.en: He went in and out of that shop all the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳을 아주 자주 드나든다는 뜻의 과장 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration meaning someone visits a place extremely often.
phrases.en_equiv: wear a path to the door

explain_en: It means almost the same as '문턱', and '문턱' is more common in daily talk. It often appears in old sayings from elders like 'don't step on the threshold'. The figurative '문턱이 높다' (hard to get into) is best learned with '문턱'.

examples.en: At the hospital, I first filled out a medical questionnaire.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 문진을 하고 나서 검사를 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor asked me questions first and then ran a test.

examples.ko: 문진 때 알레르기가 있다고 꼭 말하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to say you have allergies during the medical interview.
I did the health interview online before my checkup.

examples.ko: 문진표에 먹는 약을 모두 적어 주세요.
examples.en: Please write all the medicine you take on the questionnaire.
When the interview is over, go into the examination room.

explain: 병원에서 몸을 직접 보기 전에 증상, 병력, 알레르기 등을 묻는 과정을 말해요. 종이로 쓰는 질문지는 '문진표'라고 해서 병원이나 건강검진에서 자주 만나요. '문진을 받다', '문진을 하다'로 외워 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the step where a hospital asks about your symptoms, history and allergies before examining you. The paper form is called '문진표', which you often meet at hospitals and health checkups. It is handy to remember it as '문진을 받다' (undergo) and '문진을 하다' (conduct).

examples.ko: 우리 반은 졸업할 때 문집을 만들었어요.
examples.en: Our class made an anthology when we graduated.
I was happy that my poem was published in the anthology.

examples.ko: 이 문집은 학생들이 직접 쓴 글을 모았어요.
examples.en: This anthology collects writing that the students wrote themselves.

examples.ko: 문집 표지는 미술 동아리 친구가 그렸어요.
examples.en: A friend from the art club drew the cover of the anthology.

examples.ko: 선생님이 우리 글을 엮어 문집으로 내셨어요.
examples.en: Our teacher gathered our writing and published it as an anthology.
Last year's anthology is still on the bookshelf.

explain: 학교나 동아리에서 학생들의 글을 모아 만든 책을 말할 때 자주 써요. 한 사람의 글을 모은 책에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 졸업 문집처럼 함께 만든 책이 먼저 떠올라요. '시집'은 시만, '문집'은 여러 종류의 글을 모은 책이에요.
explain_en: It is often used for a book of writing collected at a school or club. It can also mean one person's collected works, but in daily life people first think of a graduation anthology made together. '시집' holds only poems, while '문집' gathers many kinds of writing.

examples.en: After moving in, I put a nameplate on the front gate.
The name is written in big letters on the nameplate.
The old nameplate was worn out, so we replaced it.

examples.ko: 집을 찾을 때 문패 번호를 확인하세요.
examples.en: When you look for the house, check the number on the nameplate.

examples.ko: 문패는 대문 옆 벽에 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The nameplate is attached to the wall next to the gate.

examples.ko: 요즘 아파트에는 문패가 없는 집이 많아요.
examples.en: These days, many apartment homes have no nameplate.

explain: 집 대문이나 현관 옆에 달아 두는 이름이나 주소 표시예요. 요즘 아파트는 호수만 쓰는 경우가 많아서 문패는 주로 단독주택에서 볼 수 있어요. 가게나 사무실의 이름표는 보통 '간판'이나 '명패'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the name or address sign hung by the gate or front door of a house. Apartments often show only a unit number, so nameplates are mostly seen on detached houses. For shops and offices, people usually say '간판' (signboard) or '명패' (desk or door name plate) instead.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 재미도 있고 문학성도 높아요.
examples.en: This novel is fun and also has high literary value.
That writer was recognized for literary quality.

examples.ko: 심사위원들은 작품의 문학성을 가장 중요하게 봤어요.
examples.en: The judges valued the literary quality of the work most.
People judge the literary value of web novels differently.
I want to write something with literary quality.

examples.ko: 문학성이 떨어진다고 해서 나쁜 책은 아니에요.
examples.en: A book with less literary value isn't necessarily a bad book.

explain: 작품이 문학으로서 예술적 가치가 있는지 말할 때 써요. 흔히 '재미'나 '대중성'과 나란히 놓고 비교해요. '문학적'은 분위기나 표현이 문학 같다는 느낌에도 쓰지만 '문학성'은 작품 평가에 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when talking about whether a work has artistic value as literature, and is often compared with 'fun' or popular appeal. '문학적' can also describe a literary feel or style, but '문학성' appears more when evaluating a work.

examples.ko: 오리는 발에 물갈퀴가 있어서 헤엄을 잘 쳐요.
examples.en: Ducks have webbed feet, so they swim well.

examples.ko: 수영할 때 물갈퀴처럼 생긴 장갑을 꼈어요.
examples.en: I wore gloves shaped like webbed hands when I swam.

examples.ko: 물갈퀴만 있으면 사람도 오리처럼 빨리 헤엄칠까요?
examples.en: If people had webbed feet, could we swim as fast as ducks?

examples.ko: 물갈퀴는 헤엄칠 때 물을 힘껏 밀어 줘요.
examples.en: Webbed feet push the water hard when swimming.

examples.ko: 백조 발에서도 물갈퀴를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see webbing on a swan's feet too.

examples.ko: 오리는 물갈퀴로 물을 밀면서 앞으로 나가요.
examples.en: Ducks move forward by pushing the water with their webbed feet.

explain: 오리, 개구리 같은 동물의 발가락 사이에 있는 얇은 막이에요. 사람이 수영할 때 신는 '오리발'도 모양이 비슷해서 가끔 물갈퀴라고 부르기도 해요. 보통은 동물 이야기에서 가장 많이 만나요.
explain_en: It is the thin skin between the toes of animals like ducks and frogs. Swim fins, called '오리발', look similar, so people sometimes call them '물갈퀴' too. You will meet it mostly when talking about animals.

examples.en: This meeting opened the way for dialogue.
Water trickles out of the paddy's water outlet.
That one remark became the start of the negotiation.

examples.ko: 화해의 물꼬를 트기 위해 먼저 연락해 봤어요.
examples.en: I contacted them first to break the ice and start making up.

examples.ko: 대화의 물꼬만 트이면 문제는 쉽게 풀려요.
examples.en: Once the conversation gets started, the problem is easily solved.
The water outlet in the paddy ridge broke and the water overflowed.

explain: 원래는 논에 물이 드나들게 만든 작은 통로인데, 요즘은 뉴스나 일상에서 '물꼬를 트다' 꼴로 훨씬 자주 써요. 일이나 대화가 막힌 데서 처음 풀리기 시작하는 계기를 말해요. 보통 '대화', '협상', '화해', '교류' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: The two companies opened the way for cooperation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막혀 있던 일이나 관계가 풀리기 시작하는 계기를 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means creating the first opening that lets a stuck matter or relationship begin to move.
phrases.en_equiv: break the ice; open the way

explain_en: It originally means a small passage that lets water in and out of a rice paddy, but today it is far more often used in the form '물꼬를 트다'. It refers to the first step that starts to unblock a stuck matter. It usually appears with words like dialogue, negotiation, reconciliation and exchange.

examples.en: The banana got too mushy, so I don't want to eat it.
The tomatoes went soft in the fridge.
If you boil potatoes for a long time, they get soft.
Eat the peaches before they get soft.
I cut off the soft part of the pear and eat the rest.
I picked firm apples that don't get soft.

explain: 과일이나 채소가 시간이 지나거나 익어서 단단함이 없어질 때 써요. 기본형 '무르다'는 '르' 불규칙이라 '물러요', '물러졌어요'처럼 변해요. 반대말은 '단단하다'이고, 좋은 뜻으로 부드럽게 익었을 때보다 너무 말랑해서 상했다는 느낌이 있을 때 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when fruit or vegetables lose their firmness because of time or ripening. The base verb '무르다' is a '르' irregular, so it becomes '물러요' and '물러졌어요'. The opposite is '단단하다', and it often carries the feeling of being too soft or going bad.

examples.en: The boiled potatoes cooked until soft.
A ripe persimmon feels soft when you touch it.
I boiled it too long, so the noodles got mushy.

examples.ko: 이 푸딩은 너무 물렁물렁해서 모양이 안 잡혀요.
examples.en: This pudding is so mushy that it won't hold its shape.

examples.ko: 물렁물렁한 바나나는 빵을 만들 때 쓰면 좋아요.
examples.en: Mushy bananas are good to use when baking bread.
If a pear is mushy, it has gone bad inside.

explain: '물렁물렁하다'로 훨씬 자주 쓰고, 단단하지 않고 푹 눌리는 느낌이에요. '말랑말랑'은 기분 좋게 부드러운 느낌이고, '물렁물렁'은 너무 무른 느낌이 들 때가 많아요. 반대는 '단단하다'이고, 사람에게 '물렁하다'라고 하면 성격이 약하고 만만하다는 말로 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used far more often as '물렁물렁하다', and it describes something that is not firm and gives way when pressed. '말랑말랑' feels pleasantly soft, while '물렁물렁' often feels too soft. The opposite is '단단하다', and calling a person '물렁하다' can sound like they are weak or easy to push around.

examples.ko: 경찰은 물리력을 쓰지 않고 시위대를 설득했어요.
examples.en: The police persuaded the protesters without using physical force.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 물리력보다 대화로 문제를 풀고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: That country wants to solve the problem by talking rather than by force.
An attitude of trying to settle things by force is not good.

examples.ko: 그는 물리력이 아니라 말로 사람들을 움직였어요.
examples.en: He moved people with words, not with force.
The use of physical force is strictly limited by law.
They proposed negotiating without relying on force.

explain: 뉴스나 정치, 법 이야기에서 힘으로 막거나 누르는 것을 가리킬 때 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '힘'이나 '완력'이라고 해요. '물리력 행사', '물리력을 동원하다'처럼 한자어 동사와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in news, politics and law to refer to stopping or pressing someone with force. In daily life people just say '힘' or '완력'. It often appears in set phrases like '물리력 행사' (use of force) and '물리력을 동원하다' (mobilize force).

examples.ko: 두 나라는 물밑에서 계속 협상하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries keep negotiating behind the scenes.

examples.ko: 물밑 접촉 끝에 드디어 합의가 나왔어요.
examples.en: After behind-the-scenes contacts, an agreement was finally reached.
The news spread quickly under the surface.

examples.ko: 물밑 작업 덕분에 일이 순조롭게 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the groundwork behind the scenes, things went smoothly.
The diver carefully examined the area under the water.
A reporter was the first to notice the activity beneath the surface.

explain: 뉴스에서는 대부분 '물밑 협상', '물밑 접촉', '물밑 작업'처럼 겉으로 드러나지 않게 진행하는 일을 말해요. 반대 느낌은 '수면 위로 드러나다', '공개적으로'예요. 물속 아래라는 원래 뜻도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 비유로 더 많이 들어요.
explain_en: In the news it is mostly used in phrases like '물밑 협상' (behind-the-scenes talks), '물밑 접촉' and '물밑 작업' for things done out of public view. The opposite feel is '수면 위로 드러나다' (come to the surface) or doing something publicly. It also literally means under the water, but you hear the figurative use more in daily talk.

examples.en: The heavy rain turned the whole street into a sea of water.
A bathroom pipe burst and the house is flooded.
After the typhoon passed, the village turned into a flooded area.

examples.ko: 아이가 욕조 물을 틀어 놓아 바닥이 물바다였어요.
examples.en: The child left the bath water running, and the floor was covered in water.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 물바다 같던 운동장이 말랐어요.
examples.en: When the rain stopped, the schoolyard that looked like a lake dried up.

examples.ko: 물바다에 잠긴 차를 보고 말문이 막혔어요.
examples.en: I was speechless seeing the car submerged in the floodwater.

explain: 물이 넘쳐서 바닥이나 땅이 온통 물에 덮인 모습을 말해요. 큰 홍수뿐 아니라 집에서 물을 쏟았을 때도 '완전 물바다야'처럼 조금 과장해서 말해요. '홍수'는 큰 자연재해 이름이고, '물바다'는 그 모습을 그리는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes ground or floors completely covered with overflowing water. It is used for big floods but also, a bit exaggerated, when you spill water at home, as in '완전 물바다야'. '홍수' names a big natural disaster, while '물바다' paints the picture of how it looks.

examples.en: When the boat passed, spray rose high.
The waves hit the rocks and threw up spray.
My clothes got soaked in the waterfall's spray.
A rainbow was visible through the spray.
The boat disappeared, leaving only white spray behind.
Spray sparkles when it catches the sunlight.

explain: 파도, 폭포, 배, 수영할 때 물이 부서져 흩어지며 튀어 오르는 작은 물방울들이에요. '물방울'은 하나하나의 방울이고, '물보라'는 여러 방울이 흩날리는 모습 전체를 말해요. '물보라를 일으키다', '물보라가 튀다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the many small droplets that break up and fly into the air from waves, waterfalls, boats or swimming. '물방울' is a single drop, while '물보라' is the whole scene of droplets scattering. Common patterns are '물보라를 일으키다' (throw up spray) and '물보라가 튀다' (spray splashes).

examples.ko: 그는 아들을 위해서라면 물불을 가리지 않아요.
examples.en: He will do anything at all for his son.

examples.ko: 돈을 벌려고 물불 안 가리고 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked with no thought for the hardship to earn money.

examples.ko: 물불도 안 가리는 사람이라 말리기 어려워요.
examples.en: He's a person who stops at nothing, so he's hard to stop.

examples.ko: 친구를 구하려고 물불 가리지 않고 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: He ran off without a second thought to save his friend.
I applied everywhere, willing to do whatever it took to get a job.
If you charge in recklessly, you'll get badly hurt.

explain: 거의 '물불을 가리지 않다' 꼴로 나와요. 물이든 불이든 따지지 않는다는 뜻이라 위험이나 어려움을 신경 쓰지 않고 덤빌 때 써요. 가족이나 친구를 위해서면 헌신하는 느낌이고, 돈이나 이익을 위해서면 수단을 안 가린다는 비난으로 들려요.

phrases.example: 엄마는 아이 일이라면 물불을 가리지 않으세요.
phrases.en: My mom will do anything when it comes to her child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이든 불이든 따지지 않는다는 비유로, 위험이나 어려움을 신경 쓰지 않고 달려든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor of not caring whether it is water or fire; it means rushing in regardless of danger or difficulty.
phrases.en_equiv: go through fire and water; stop at nothing

explain_en: It almost always appears as '물불을 가리지 않다'. Water or fire makes no difference, so it is used for rushing in regardless of danger or difficulty. For family or friends it sounds devoted; for money or profit it sounds like using any means.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 노래를 부르다니 참 물색없네요.
examples.en: Singing in the middle of a meeting is so out of place.
Everyone went quiet because of the tactless joke.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 눈치도 없고 물색없어서 자주 혼나요.
examples.en: That friend is clueless and out of touch, so he often gets scolded.

examples.ko: 분위기도 모르고 그런 말을 하다니 물색없어요.
examples.en: Saying that without reading the mood is really tactless.
I'm sorry if I was out of line.

examples.ko: 물색없게 들릴지 몰라도 한 가지만 물어볼게요.
examples.en: It might sound tactless, but let me ask just one thing.

explain: 상황이나 분위기에 맞지 않게 말하거나 행동해서 어색할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '눈치 없다'가 더 흔하고, '물색없다'는 조금 글 같거나 점잖게 지적하는 느낌이에요. 보통 사람의 말이나 행동을 평가할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used when someone speaks or acts in a way that doesn't fit the situation or mood. In daily speech '눈치 없다' is more common, while '물색없다' sounds a bit bookish or like a polite criticism. It is usually used to judge a person's words or actions.

examples.ko: 그는 회의 중에 물색없이 웃음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: He burst out laughing at an inappropriate moment during the meeting.
I'm sorry for butting in at a bad time.

examples.ko: 동생이 물색없이 비싼 선물을 사 와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that my younger sibling bought an absurdly expensive gift for no good reason.
Don't butt into other people's conversations at the wrong moment.

examples.ko: 물색없이 큰 소리로 떠들면 눈총을 받아요.
examples.en: If you chatter loudly at the wrong time, you'll get dirty looks.
Why are you behaving so tactlessly?

explain: 때와 장소를 가리지 않고 엉뚱하게 행동하는 모습을 말해요. '뜬금없이'는 갑작스러운 것에 초점이 있고, '물색없이'는 분위기에 안 맞는다는 비난이 더 들어 있어요. '눈치 없이'라고도 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: It describes acting out of place without regard for time or setting. '뜬금없이' focuses on suddenness, while '물색없이' carries more criticism of not fitting the mood. People also say '눈치 없이' in a similar way.

examples.ko: 경비가 물샐틈없어서 아무도 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Security is airtight, so nobody can get in.

examples.ko: 물샐틈없는 준비 덕분에 행사가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the meticulous preparation, the event ended well.
That team's defense is really airtight.

examples.ko: 계획이 물샐틈없다고 해도 변수는 생기기 마련이에요.
examples.en: Even if a plan is airtight, unexpected things are bound to happen.
Even the watertight guard had a small gap.
Lock up the doors tightly before you leave.

explain: '빈틈없다'와 비슷하지만 경비, 경계, 방어, 준비처럼 막거나 지키는 일에 더 자주 써요. 물 한 방울도 샐 틈이 없다는 비유라 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 가볍게 쓰기보다 뉴스나 이야기에서 꽤 힘줘서 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '빈틈없다' (no gaps) but is used more for guarding or blocking things such as security, watch, defense and preparation. The image of not letting even a drop of water through makes it feel strong. It is less for casual talk and more for news or emphatic speech.

examples.en: The police guarded the area around the venue without a single gap.
I prepared the documents thoroughly, so don't worry.
I locked the doors and windows tightly.
He drew up every plan down to the last detail.
Even though I sealed it tightly, water still leaks.
Airport security is being carried out without any gaps.

explain: '철저히', '빈틈없이'와 비슷하지만, 막고 지키고 준비하는 모습에 쓰면 더 생생해요. 보통 '지키다', '막다', '준비하다', '짜다' 같은 동사 앞에 나와요. 형용사 '물샐틈없다'가 '-이'로 바뀐 부사예요.
explain_en: It resembles '철저히' and '빈틈없이' but is more vivid when describing guarding, blocking or preparing. It typically comes before verbs like '지키다', '막다', '준비하다' and '짜다'. It is the adverb form of the adjective '물샐틈없다'.

examples.en: I skipped stones across the lake.

examples.ko: 납작한 돌로 하면 물수제비가 잘 떠져요.
examples.en: Stone skipping works well with a flat stone.
I can't even skip a stone, which is embarrassing.
We held a stone skipping contest at the stream.
Flat stones are best for skipping.
The stone flew off bouncing like a skipping stone.

explain: 납작한 돌을 수면에 던져 통통 튀게 하는 놀이예요. 보통 '물수제비를 뜨다'라고 하는데, '뜨다'가 이 놀이에만 쓰이는 짝말이라 같이 외우세요. 먹는 '수제비'와 이름이 닮았지만, 이 말은 돌 던지기 놀이를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is the game of throwing a flat stone so that it bounces across the water. People say '물수제비를 뜨다', and '뜨다' here is a set partner verb, so learn them together. The name looks like the food '수제비', but this word refers to the stone-throwing game.
